title: ASEAN, Australia eye stronger trade, maritime security
summary: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and Australia on Monday committed to strengthening two-way trade and investment and continuing cooperation on maritime security.

blocks.text: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and Australia on Monday committed to strengthening two-way trade and investment and continuing cooperation on maritime security.

During the 6th ASEAN-Australia Summit, President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. said Australia, ASEAN's first dialogue partner, had long supported the region's efforts to advance peace, prosperity and sustainable development.
“Our cooperation spans maritime security, cybersecurity, counterterrorism, and the fight against trafficking in persons, online scams, and illicit drugs,” Marcos said.
The President also highlighted the growing economic ties between ASEAN and Australia.
“Two-way trade reached AUD197.5 billion last year, and the upgraded ASEAN-Australia-New Zealand Free Trade Area gives our businesses greater market access and certainty,” Marcos said.
He also noted Australia's commitment of up to AUD15 million (about P648.2 million) for the ASEAN Centre for Public Health Emergencies and Emerging Diseases.

Marcos said Australia also supports the ASEAN Coordinating Centre for Humanitarian Assistance on Disaster Management, the new TRIANGLE Partnerships for migrant workers, and Timor-Leste's integration into ASEAN.
Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, meanwhile, vowed to continue investing in ASEAN and ASEAN-led institutions.

“Because we believe in ASEAN centrality and that this is the key to our region's success and our shared future. And because as a reliable partner, we understand that maintaining peace and stability in our region is a collective responsibility,” Albanese said.

“Together, we recommit our efforts to increasing our two-way trade and investment, harnessing the opportunities of clean energy, climate resilience, better infrastructure, fairer educational opportunities and strengthened maritime security,” he added.
Albanese said shared security and peace depended on shared economic prosperity, adding that Australia aimed to deepen its economic ties with its regional partners.
He cited Australia's Southeast Asia Economic Strategy to 2040, which he said had supported $4.5 billion in new Australian investments in ASEAN.

“We are determined to keep building on this progress and today I announce also that we will expand our investment deal teams and establish a new Invested 2040 window through Australian Development Investments, our international impact investment fund,” he said.
“These initiatives will connect Australian capital with Southeast Asia's fastest growing businesses, helping us to harness the region's next wave of economic growth,” he added.

Albanese also expressed confidence that ASEAN and Australia could continue responding to global conflicts and challenges, including the oil and energy crisis, by investing in the resilience of their shared energy supply chains.— MCG, GMA News
